programs.name: Zimislecel (VX-880)
programs.modality: Fully differentiated stem-cell-derived islets, infused into the portal vein
programs.population: T1D with impaired hypoglycemia awareness and severe hypoglycemia
programs.summary: Phase 1/2/3 master protocol (FORWARD). In the NEJM report, 10 of 12 full-dose participants were insulin-independent at day 365; all 12 had HbA1c <7% and no severe hypoglycemia. Requires chronic immunosuppression; two deaths were reported in the study (cryptococcal meningitis; progression of pre-existing neurocognitive disease). Vertex postponed completion of dosing in Jan 2026 for an internal manufacturing analysis, then resumed dosing; it said it will give updated timelines later in 2026.
programs.reality_check: The strongest cure-type data in the field, but it's a swap of insulin for lifelong immunosuppression, aimed first at the sickest ~60k patients. The 2026 filing goal has slipped and has no new date yet.

programs.name: Teplizumab (Tzield; Teizeild in EU)
programs.modality: Anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody, 14-day IV course
programs.population: Stage 2 T1D age 8+ (full approval); recently diagnosed stage 3 T1D age 8–17 (accelerated approval, Jun 2026)
programs.summary: FDA-approved (Nov 2022) to delay stage 3 T1D in stage 2 patients age 8+, based on TN-10 (median delay of about 2 years). EU approval came in Jan 2026. On Jun 12, 2026 the FDA granted accelerated approval to slow the decline of insulin production in children age 8–17 recently diagnosed with stage 3 T1D. That approval rests on a C-peptide surrogate endpoint, and a post-approval study must confirm clinical benefit. In the earlier PROTECT Phase 3 (new-onset), teplizumab met its C-peptide primary endpoint but did not separate on clinical secondary endpoints. A new Phase 3 (βETA PRESERVE, age 1–25) is enrolling.
programs.reality_check: It's the only approved disease-modifying T1D drug, and now it's approved both before and just after diagnosis. It slows the disease rather than curing it, and the new-onset label is accelerated on a surrogate endpoint. If the confirmatory study fails, the FDA can withdraw it.
